item.title: Dave Täht given the Jonathan B. Postel Service Award
item.dc:creator: corbet
item.description:
The Internet Society has announced that the Jonathan B. Postel Service Award has been awarded to Dave Täht for his many efforts to improve the Internet.

Täht's legacy can be found in community hubs in Nicaragua, where he worked to expand connectivity, and first discovered the urgency of solving bufferbloat. It can be found in every lag-free video call with a loved one. It can be found in outer space—Täht helped Starlink solve its latency challenges. And it can be found in the countless people he mentored and befriended over the years, who will not stop until bufferbloat stops getting in the way of band practice.

Dave is still deeply missed by those of us who knew him; this is an award he richly deserved.

item.title: Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS released
item.dc:creator: jzb
item.description:
System76 has announced the release of Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS, which is based on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. Notable features in this release include drawing tablet support, automatic updates, a number of new COSMIC applications, and more. Updates for users on Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS will be enabled in December.

LWN last covered Pop!_OS and an early version of its COSMIC desktop in August 2024.

item.title: Firefox 161.0 released
item.dc:creator: jzb
item.description: Version 161.0 of the Firefox web browser has been released. Notable changes in this release include the ability to assign a shortcut to copy the current tab's URL, addition of a menu item for Tab Groups, and the built-in VPN can be turned off or on for specific sites. There are also a number of security fixes in this release.

item.title: CachyOS November 2026 release
item.dc:creator: jzb
item.description: CachyOS, a performance-focused distribution based on Arch Linux, has announced its November 2026 release. Notable changes in this release include a new recovery environment ("cachyos-recovery") for rolling back broken systems, Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) v2 support for games that require EAC to run, version 2.0.0 of the CachyOS Package Installer, and more.

item.title: Seven stable kernels for Monday
item.dc:creator: jzb
item.description: Greg Kroah-Hartman has announced the 7.3.6, 6.18.65, 6.12.119, 6.6.163, 6.1.193, 5.15.226, and 5.10.275 stable kernels. Each of these contains quite a few patches throughout the tree—6.12.119 has the fewest with more than 1,700 patches, while 6.6.163 has more than 3,300. Users are advised to upgrade.

item.title: Kernel prepatch 7.4-rc4
item.dc:creator: jzb
item.description: The 7.4-rc4 kernel is out for testing. Linus said: "It's huge. What a surprise. Lots of little fixes all over, with drivers being pretty exactly half of it (gpu and networking showing up as usual, but there's usb, iio, nvme, sound.. you name it)."

item.title: Beyls: Wrapping up LLVM's relicensing effort
item.dc:creator: jzb
item.description:
Kristof Beyls has published a summary to the LLVM discussion forum to announce that the project is declaring success and bringing its relicensing effort to a close after eight years.

We've been asking past contributors to relicense their work since 2018. New contributions have come in under Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception since January 19, 2019. Code contributed before that date was under LLVM's earlier licenses (UIUC/NCSA, plus MIT for some runtime libraries), so we needed permission from its authors to move it over. [...]

Today, more than 99.5% of all lines of code ever contributed to LLVM are either covered by the new license, too small for copyright to apply, or no longer in the repository.

Rather than trying to "chase the last tiny fraction forever" LLVM is winding up the effort. Any contributors with code contributed before January 19, 2019 who have not signed a relicensing agreement and do not want their contributions made available under Apache-2.0 with the LLVM-exception can still reach out to the project to ensure their code has the appropriate SPDX license identifier.

item.title: Vim Classic 8.3.1 released
item.dc:creator: jzb
item.description:
Version 8.3.1 of Vim Classic—a long-term support fork of Vim maintained without LLM assistance—has been released.

This release includes applicable Vim patches up to Vim 8.2.3237, including numerous bug fixes, minor features, and compatibility improvements for Vim plugins. This release also removes Python 2 support from Vim Classic.

The full list of changes in this release is available on sourcehut.
